item on the agenda or any other topic.

Watch or Listen: Meetings are broadcast/streamed live on the City of Commerce’s Facebook:
https://www.facebook.com/City-of-Commerce-123903054365151/?ref . Archived, on-demand  video  of  each  meeting
is maintained on the City’s Facebook as part of the public record.

2. Submit Comments before the Meeting: Members of the public can provide public comment by sending an

PUBLIC COMMENT
Citizens wishing to address the City Council and Successor Agency on any item on the agenda or on any matter
not on the agenda may do so at this time. State law (Government Code Section 54950 et seq.) prohibits the City
Council from taking action or engaging in discussion on a specific item unless it appears on a posted agenda .
Upon request, the City Council may, in their discretion, allow citizen participation on a specific item on the agenda
at the time the item is considered by the City Council. If you wish to address the City Council /Successor Agency
at this time, please complete a speaker's card and give it to the City Clerk prior to commencement of the City
Council meeting. Please limit your remarks to three (3) minutes.

To increase the effectiveness of the Public Comment Period, the following rules shall be followed: No person shall
make any remarks which result in disrupting, disturbing or otherwise impeding the meeting.

  CONSENT CALENDAR
Items under the Consent Calendar are considered to be routine and may be enacted by one motion. There will be
no discussion of these items unless members of the Public or City Council request specific items to be removed
from the Consent Agenda for a separate discussion. lf the item is desired to be discussed separately, it should be
the first item under Scheduled Matters.

minutes_text:
AGENDA ITEMS AND ACTIONS
5:00 P.M. CLOSED SESSION

CALL TO ORDER Mayor Argumedo called meeting to order at 5:03 p.m.

ROLL CALL

PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION ITEMS There were no individuals wishing to address the City Council on any items on Closed Session agenda. 

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION City Council recessed to Closed session at 5:04 p.m.

RECONVENE TO OPEN SESSION City Council/ Successor Agency reconvened to Open Session at 6:19 p.m.

ORAL CLOSED SESSION ANNOUNCEMENT City Attorney Tapia reported on Closed Session items: 

Items #1 and #2 - City staff made a presentation, City Council provided direction and no reportable action was taken on these items. 

Item #3  - City staff made a presentation, and no reportable action was taken on this item.    


6:00 P.M. - CITY COUNCIL MEETING

CALL TO ORDER Mayor Argumedo called regular City Council meeting to order at 6:21 p.m.

ROLL CALL

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE Director of Parks and Recreation Alaniz led the Pledge of Allegiance.

INVOCATION Councilmember Rebollo offered the invocation. 

APPEARANCES AND PRESENTATIONS

6.. Presentation/Update from the Sheriff's Department Regarding Public Safety in the City of Commerce Sergeant Duarte presented a summary of the events and activities that occurred over the past two weeks. This included a homeless clean-up operation and an overview of the various meetings herself and Deputies had attended, such as the State of the City address and a town hall meeting at the Senior Center. Sergeant Duarte  also reported attending a concert in the park, noting that there were no issues or incidents during the event.

In response to the presentation, Councilmember Lainez expressed appreciation for the comprehensive overview of the recent activities. Councilmember Lainez also inquired about the progress of the recruitment for the Public Safety Manager position, to which City Manager Cisneros responded that the recruitment process is still ongoing.


1.. Proclamation Declaring September 2023 as Deaf Awareness Month in the City of Commerce Director of Parks and Recreation, Mr. Alaniz, delivered a presentation. In response, Janelle Ocampo expressed her gratitude towards the dedicated parks and recreation staff for offering a diverse array of programs catering to children with hearing impairments. She shared that her daughter Samantha had the chance to participate in some of these programs, most notably embarking on her journey in volleyball. Ms. Ocampo extended her heartfelt thanks to the City for its commendable efforts.

Samantha Ocampo herself took a moment to convey her appreciation to both the City Council and the Parks staff for the numerous opportunities they had provided her.

Mayor Argumedo then proceeded to read an official proclamation.

Councilmember Rebollo took the opportunity to offer her comments and express gratitude to the Ocampo family for being a continual source of inspiration. Councilmember Rebollo specifically commended Samantha for her remarkable courage in addressing the Council.


2.. Commendation Honoring Cindy Montañez for Her Leadership  as the CEO of TreePeople USA and Contributions to the City of Commerce, County of Los Angeles, and State of California This item was continued to the next City Council meeting. 

PUBLIC COMMENT There were no individuals wishing to address the City Council.  




CONSENT CALENDAR  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Oralia Rebollo

4.. Approval of Minutes

5.. Competitive Tree Planting Grant Program - First Amendment to Deed Restriction

3.. Approval of Warrant Register Nos. 24A, 24B, 3A and 3B

SCHEDULED MATTERS

8.. Committee and Commission Appointments Councilmember Rebollo appointed Smyrna Caraveo to the Education Commission. 

Vice Mayor Altamirano asked that the vacancy on Senior Commission is advertised.  

7.. Amending the Annual Operating Budget for Fiscal Year 2023-2024  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Mireya Garcia City Manager Cisneros indicated that although some aspects are still being finalized and discussions with the City Council are ongoing, there was a request for approval of certain timely capital outlay items. The remaining items would be brought before the Council at a later date.

If the requested items were to be approved during tonight's meeting, it would result in a surplus of 5.7 million dollars.

The items that were requested for approval included personnel requests for a full-time Permit Technician, a full-time Code Enforcement Officer, a full-time Maintenance Specialist, two full-time Street Maintenance Workers, and two part-time Class Instructors. Additionally, funds would be allocated for a traveling team, capital outlay items such as furnishings for the library and Camp Commerce, as well as transportation items including a Ford Transit Van, a JCB compact track loader, two DAR electric vehicles, and an outdoor forklift. The total for these items amounted to $785,190 dollars.






ORDINANCES

9.. Second Reading of an Uncodified Ordinance Approving a Development Agreement Related to Application No. 18-052  -  Action: approve (Pass) Moved by Oralia Rebollo City Manager Cisneros left the Council Chambers during this item.  Director of Administrative Services and City Clerk provided a brief overview.  

CITY COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY REPORTS Councilmember Garcia had the pleasure of attending the Concert in the Park and described it as a very well organized event.

Councilmember Rebollo participated in the Contract Cities meeting and expressed her request for detailed information regarding Measure H, including the total amount of funds received and a breakdown of their allocation. She further expressed her intention to schedule a meeting with Sergeant and the public safety staff to gain a better understanding of upcoming public safety measures in the upcoming election. Councilmember Rebollo issued her condolences to Celia Hinojosa' family.

Councilmember Lainez shared his attendance at the Rosewood Park banquet for soccer athletes, the event hosted by Congressman Robert Garcia at the Senior Center, which he praised as a well-organized town hall meeting Councilmember Lainez also reported his attendance and praised well-organized the Concert in the Park.

Mayor Argumedo reported on his attendance at the town hall meeting organized by Congressman Robert Garcia, where he delivered a welcoming speech, and also his presence at the Summer Concert Series.


ADJOURNMENT Meeting adjourned at 7:30pm  in memory of Celia Hinojosa.

Written materials distributed to the City Council are available for public inspection immediately following the posting of this agenda (at least 72 hours prior to a regular City Council meetings) in the City Clerk's Office, at Commerce City Hall, 2535 Commerce Way, Commerce, California, and the Central Library, 5655 Jillson Street, Commerce, California.

Meeting facilities are accessible to persons with disabilities. ln compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, notify the Office of the City Clerk at (323) 722-4805 at least 24 hours prior to the meeting.
